comments.body:
**Note from #637's re-plan (2026-09-12): the client Abort here and #664's restore fence should share one fence batch.**

#664 (637.4) makes restore fence every session a restored image brings back. An `Open@E` session goes to `Aborting@E+1`, with its `retire:bytes` obligation in the same batch (the abort/reap row, `0016:664`). A `Completing` session takes the `Completing → Aborting` row instead (`0016:665`). The client Abort in this issue crosses the same `Open → Aborting` edge, so the two should use one batch builder, not two.

Whichever lands first builds it, and the other reuses it. #664's brief constrains the builder to produce only obligations that `decode_retire_obligation` accepts against the key they are written under. `RetirePayload` withholds a writer-side constructor on purpose (`crates/core/src/multipart.rs:3036-3060`), so this is the rule any first writer has to meet.

Flag from #842 (routed by the wyrd-pdca Act review of 2026-09-30): proposal 0016's reaper and operator-abort `Completing → Aborting` rows (`0016:665`, `:2193`) still specify a `{session, parts: <set>}` retirement payload. That shape exceeds `MAX_VALUE_BYTES` for a sparse session: 10,000 sparse parts = 128,916 bytes > 100,000, and FoundationDB refuses it permanently. #842's restore fence avoids it for this reason (`crates/core/src/multipart.rs` ~3302 and the row above it). #842 did not edit 0016. When #656/#659 build these writers, use `{session, all}` as the Open fence does, or pre-check with `flat_value_ceiling_crossed` and name the session unsettled. Same note applies to #659.
